dice.title: Dice and turns
dice.body:
The first game of a match starts with one die each. The higher die starts and plays those two dice. On a tie, you both roll again.
On your turn you roll two dice. Each die moves one checker forward by that many points.
You can move one checker with both dice, or two checkers with one die each.
A double counts twice: with 4-4 you play four moves of 4.
You must play both dice if you can. If you can play only one of them, play the higher one when you can.
If you have no move, your turn passes.
After that, the winner of each game starts the next one and rolls both dice.

bearOff.title: Bearing off
bearOff.body:
When all 15 of your checkers are in your home, you can bear them off.
A die bears off a checker from the point with the same number: a 4 bears off from point 4.
If that point is empty, you must move a checker from a higher point.
If you have no checker on a higher point, you bear off from your highest point.
You can also use a die to move a checker inside your home instead.

scoring.title: Points
scoring.body:
Mono (μονό): you win 1 point if the other player has borne off at least one checker.
Diplo (διπλό): you win 2 points if the other player has not borne off any checker.
The match ends when a player reaches the points you picked on New game: 1, 3, 5 or 7.
scoring.bodyPerChecker:
You win 1 point for each checker the other player has not borne off. If they have borne off none, you win 15.
A resign counts the same way: the other player wins 1 point for each checker you have not borne off.
The match ends when a player reaches the points you picked on New game: 1, 3, 5 or 7.

portes.start:
Each player has 15 checkers: 2 on point 24, 5 on point 13, 3 on point 8 and 5 on point 6.
The other player sets up the same way on their side.

moves.title: How checkers move
moves.body:
Your checkers move toward your home. The other player moves the opposite way.
A checker can land on an empty point, on your own checkers, or on a single checker of the other player.
It cannot land on a point with 2 or more of the other player's checkers. That point is a door (πόρτα).
When one checker plays both dice, it must also be able to land on the point in between.
Six doors in a row close the way completely.

hitting.title: Hitting
hitting.body:
If you land on a single checker of the other player, you hit it. It goes out to the bar in the middle of the board.
A player with a checker on the bar must bring it back in before moving any other checker.
It enters in the other player's home: a 1 enters on your point 24, a 6 on your point 19.
It cannot enter on a door. If no die can bring it in, you lose the whole turn.
When you come in, you can hit a single checker too.

portes.bearOff: If one of your checkers is hit while you bear off, bring it back home before you bear off again.

plakoto.goal: There is no hitting in Plakoto. You pin the other player's checkers instead.
plakoto.start:
Each player starts with all 15 checkers on point 24, their starting point.
The other player's stack sits on your point 1, inside your home.

moves.title: How checkers move
moves.body:
Your checkers move toward your home. The other player moves the opposite way.
A checker can land on an empty point, on your own checkers, or on a single checker of the other player.
It cannot land on 2 or more of the other player's checkers, or where the other player pins one of yours. Those points are doors (πόρτες).
When one checker plays both dice, it must also be able to land on the point in between.
Checkers never leave the board and never move back.

pinning.title: Pinning (πλάκωμα)
pinning.body:
If you land on a single checker of the other player, you pin it: your checker sits on top.
A pinned checker cannot move. It is free again only when all checkers on top of it have left.
You can move off the pinned checker at any time, or put more checkers on top.
A checker that pins cannot be pinned.

plakoto.bearOff: You cannot bear off while any of your checkers is pinned, even one inside your home.

mother.title: The mother (μάνα)
mother.body:
Your mother is your last checker on point 24, once all the others have left.
If the other player pins your mother, you choose at the end of their turn: resign or play on.
Resign: the other player wins 2 points (diplo) and the game ends.
Play on: the game goes on as normal. You are not asked again in this game.
Your mother is free again only when the other player's checkers leave it. Until then you cannot bear off.
If both mothers are pinned at the same time, the game is a draw. Nobody gets points, and the next game starts again with one die each.
Keep 2 or more checkers on point 24, and nobody can pin your mother.

fevga.goal: There is no hitting and no pinning in Fevga. It is a race.
fevga.start:
Each player starts with all 15 checkers on point 24, their starting point.
The two stacks sit in opposite corners. The other player's stack is on your point 12.

moves.title: How checkers move
moves.body:
Both players move the same way around the board, each toward their own home.
A checker can land only on an empty point or on your own checkers.
When one checker plays both dice, it must also be able to land on the point in between.

noHitting.title: No hitting
noHitting.body:
You never hit or pin in Fevga.
One checker is enough to hold a point: the other player can never land there.
So you block the other player by holding the points in front of them.

runner.title: The first checker
runner.body:
At the start you may move only one checker: your runner.
No other checker can leave point 24 until the runner has passed the other player's mother (μάνα), on your point 12. Then you can move any checker.
This can happen in the middle of your turn: once the runner has passed, your other dice can move any checker.
If the runner cannot move, you lose the rest of the roll.

primes.title: Six in a row (εξάπορτο)
primes.body:
You may not hold six points in a row in your starting quarter (points 19 to 24).
You may not hold six points in a row right in front of the other player's mother (your points 6 to 11).
This counts at the end of your turn. If the only way to play both dice breaks it, you play one die only.
Six in a row anywhere else is fine, but you must leave the other player a move if you can.
If every play you have blocks the other player, you can play any of them, and they pass.

asodio.goal: In Asodio your 15 checkers move as one army, quarter by quarter. There is no hitting: you pin, as in Plakoto.
asodio.start:
All 15 checkers start off the board. The board is empty.
Your checkers wait next to your starting quarter (points 19 to 24). A number shows how many are still to enter.

moves.title: How checkers move
moves.body:
Your checkers move toward your home. The other player moves the opposite way.
When one checker plays both dice, it must also be able to land on the point in between.
Once a checker is on the board, it stays there until you bear it off, and it never moves back.

entering.title: Entering (ασόδυο)
entering.body:
The board is locked until you roll a 1-2 (ασόδυο) or a double. Any other roll does nothing, and the turn passes.
Each die enters one checker in your starting quarter: a 1 on point 24, a 2 on point 23, and so on up to a 6 on point 19.
A double enters four checkers on the same point: with 3-3, four checkers enter on point 22.
Once the board is open, every roll enters more checkers.
Entered checkers wait: no checker moves until all 15 are on the board.
A checker cannot enter on 2 or more of the other player's checkers. If no die can enter a checker, the turn passes.

quarters.title: Quarter by quarter
quarters.body:
When all 15 checkers are on the board, the army may move on.
Your path has four quarters: points 19 to 24, 13 to 18, 7 to 12, and your home, 1 to 6.
A checker that moves into a new quarter is frozen there. It cannot move again until all 15 of your checkers have reached that quarter.
So your last checker sets the pace: move it up, and the army is free again.
On the board, frozen checkers look a little darker.

pinning.title: Pinning (πλάκωμα)
pinning.body:
If you land on a single checker of the other player, you pin it: your checker sits on top. There is no hitting.
A pinned checker cannot move. It is free again when the checkers on top of it leave.
You cannot land on 2 or more of the other player's checkers, or where they pin one of yours.
If your last checker is pinned, your whole army is frozen: you pass until it is free.

asodio.bearOff: You cannot bear off while any of your checkers is pinned.

draw.title: A draw
draw.body:
If no checker of either player can ever move again, the game is a draw.
Nobody gets points, and the next game starts again with one die each.

tavli.title: A Tavli match
tavli.body:
A Tavli match plays three games in turn: Portes, then Plakoto, then Fevga, and then Portes again.
Each game gives 1 or 2 points, as its own rules say. A Plakoto game can also end in a draw (both mothers pinned): nobody gets points, and the match goes on with the next game.
The first player to reach the match points wins.

plakotoFederation.title: This game: federation rules
plakotoFederation.body:
This game plays the federation rules (ΕΟΠΤ). Only the mother rule is different from the page below.
If you pin the other player's mother, you win 2 points (diplo) as soon as none of your checkers is left on your own point 24. Until then the game goes on, and your own mother can still be pinned.
If both mothers are pinned at the same time, the game is a draw.
Nobody is asked to resign or play on.

asodioGreek.title: This game: Greek rules
asodioGreek.body:
This game plays Acey-Deucey with the Greek rules. They change the page below:
You hit, you do not pin. A lone checker that is hit goes out, to the middle of the board. It enters again in your starting quarter, but only with a 1-2 or a double.
The board still opens only with a 1-2 or a double. After that, checkers on the board may move before all 15 are in, and no quarter freezes.
After a 1-2 you play the 1 and the 2, then choose any double and play it, then roll again.
After a double that you play in full, you roll again too.
You cannot bear off while a checker is still outside the board.

asodioAmerican.title: This game: American rules
asodioAmerican.body:
This game plays Acey-Deucey with the American rules. They change the page below:
You hit, you do not pin. A lone checker that is hit goes out, to the middle of the board, and enters again in your starting quarter.
The board is open from the start: any roll can enter checkers. Checkers on the board may move before all 15 are in, and no quarter freezes.
After a 1-2 you play the 1 and the 2, then choose any double and play it, then roll again.
The winner gets 1 point for each checker the loser has not borne off.
You cannot bear off while a checker is still outside the board.

tutorial.title: Learn to play
tutorial.skipHint: Leave the lesson. You can open it again from Settings.
tutorial.openFromRules: Learn to play on the board

move.title: Move a checker
move.body: You play the light checkers. Tap the lit checker, then tap the ring. Or drag it there. In a real game you roll the dice with a swipe on the board.
move.hint: Move the lit checker 4 points, with the 4.
move.done: Well done! A checker moves as many points as the die shows.
move.board: Board. Your checker on point 13 is lit. Dice 4 and 2. Move it 4 points, to point 9.

bothDice.title: Use both dice
bothDice.body: Each die is one move. Move the lit checker with the 5, then again with the 3.
bothDice.hint: Move the same checker again, with the other die.
bothDice.done: Good! You played both dice with one checker.
bothDice.board: Board. Your checker on point 13 is lit. Dice 5 and 3. Move it twice, one die each time.

double.title: A double moves four times
double.body: You rolled 3-3. A double plays four times. Move the lit checker four times.
double.hint: Keep moving the same checker, 3 points each time.
double.done: Four moves of 3. Doubles are strong!
double.board: Board. Your checker on point 13 is lit. Dice 3-3. Move it 3 points, four times.

makePoint.title: Make a door
makePoint.body: Two or more of your checkers on a point make a door. Your opponent cannot land there. Move both lit checkers to point 7.
makePoint.hint: Both lit checkers go to the same point: 7.
makePoint.done: Door made! Your opponent cannot land on point 7.
makePoint.board: Board. Your checkers on points 11 and 9 are lit. Dice 4 and 2. Move both to point 7.

hit.title: Hit a lone checker
hit.body: A lone checker can be hit. Land on the dark checker on point 9 to send it to the bar.
hit.hint: Move the lit checker 4 points, onto the dark checker.
hit.done: Hit! That checker must come back in from the bar.
hit.board: Board. Your checker on point 13 is lit. Your opponent has a lone checker on point 9. Dice 4 and 1.

enter.title: Enter from the bar
enter.body: Now your checker was hit and waits on the bar. It must come in, in your opponent's home, before any other move.
enter.hint: The 5 lands on a door, so it is blocked. Enter with the 3.
enter.done: You are back in! A door blocks your entry too.
enter.board: Board. Your checker is on the bar and lit. Dice 5 and 3. The 5 is blocked; the 3 enters on point 22.

bearOff.title: Bear off
bearOff.body: When all your checkers are home, you take them off the board. Bear off your last two checkers.
bearOff.hint: Tap a lit checker, then tap the ring in the tray.
bearOff.done: All 15 are off. You win the game!
bearOff.board: Board. All your checkers are home. The last two are on points 6 and 4, and lit. Dice 6 and 4.

pin.title: Pin a lone checker
pin.body: There is no hitting in Plakoto. Land on a lone dark checker and you pin it: your checker sits on top. Move the lit checker onto the dark checker on point 9.
pin.hint: Move the lit checker 4 points, onto the dark checker.
pin.done: Pinned! The dark checker stays under yours and cannot move. There is no bar in Plakoto.
pin.board: Board. Your checker on point 13 is lit. Your opponent has a lone checker on point 9. Dice 4 and 2.

pinned.title: A pinned checker waits
pinned.body: Your checker on point 16 is pinned under a dark checker. It cannot move until all checkers on top of it have left. Move the lit checker instead, with both dice.
pinned.hint: Your checker on point 16 is pinned and cannot move. Move the lit checker.
pinned.done: Good. Your checker on point 16 is free again once the dark checker leaves.
pinned.board: Board. Your checker on point 16 is pinned. Your checker on point 13 is lit. Dice 5 and 2.

mother.title: The mother (μάνα)
mother.body: A player's mother is their last checker on their start point, point 24. Your opponent's mother sits alone on your point 1. Pin it with the lit checker.
mother.hint: Move the lit checker 4 points, onto point 1.
mother.done: You pinned the mother! Now your opponent must choose.
mother.board: Board. Your checker on point 5 is lit. Your opponent's last checker sits alone on its start, your point 1. Dice 4 and 3.

plakotoBearOff.title: Bear off
plakotoBearOff.body: You bear off as in Portes, once all your checkers are home. In Plakoto, none of your checkers may be pinned. Bear off your last two checkers.
plakotoBearOff.hint: Tap a lit checker, then tap the ring in the tray.
plakotoBearOff.done: All 15 are off. You win the game!
plakotoBearOff.board: Board. All your checkers are home and none is pinned. The last two are on points 5 and 3, and lit. Dice 5 and 3.

sameWay.title: The same way round
sameWay.body: Each player starts with all 15 checkers on point 24. The two stacks sit in opposite corners: the dark stack is on your point 12. Both players move the same way round the board. Move your first checker with both dice.
sameWay.hint: Move one checker from point 24, then move the same checker again.
sameWay.done: Off it runs! The dark checkers run the same way, from your point 12.
sameWay.board: Board. Your 15 checkers are on point 24, and lit. The dark stack is on your point 12. Dice 5 and 3.

holdPoint.title: One checker holds a point
holdPoint.body: There is no hitting and no pinning in Fevga. One checker is enough to hold a point: the other player can never land there. Move the lit checker with both dice.
holdPoint.hint: The 4 lands on the dark checker on point 6. Play the 3 first, then the 4.
holdPoint.done: Right. The lone dark checker blocked the 4, so you went round it.
holdPoint.board: Board. Your checker on point 10 is lit. A lone dark checker holds point 6. Dice 4 and 3.

runner.title: The first checker
runner.body: No other checker may leave point 24 until your first checker has passed your opponent's mother, on your point 12. Move it past with the 2. Then move a checker from point 24 with the 1.
runner.hint: First the lit checker, from 13 to 11 with the 2. Then a checker from 24, with the 1.
runner.done: Your first checker passed the dark stack, so all your checkers may move now.
runner.board: Board. Your first checker, on point 13, is lit. 14 checkers wait on point 24. The dark stack is on your point 12. Dice 2 and 1.

sixInARow.title: Six in a row (εξάπορτο)
sixInARow.body: You may not hold all six of your points 19 to 24 at the end of your turn. Here a 5 from point 24 would do that, and every other way to play both dice is blocked. So you play one die, the higher one: move the lit checker with the 6.
sixInARow.hint: A 5 from point 24 makes six in a row. Move the lit checker with the 6.
sixInARow.done: The 5 is lost. Six in a row is not allowed on your points 6 to 11 either, right in front of your opponent's mother.
sixInARow.board: Board. You hold points 20 to 24. Your checker on point 8 is lit. The dark checkers hold points 13 to 18. Dice 6 and 5.

aceDeuce.title: Open the board with 1-2 (ασόδυο)
aceDeuce.body: In Asodio all 15 checkers start off the board. The board stays locked until you roll a 1-2 or a double. You rolled 1-2: the 1 enters a checker on point 24, the 2 on point 23. Tap the lit stack of waiting checkers, then a ring.
aceDeuce.hint: Tap the lit stack of waiting checkers, then the ring on point 24 or 23.
aceDeuce.done: The board is open! Any other first roll would have done nothing, and the turn would pass.
aceDeuce.board: Board. All 15 of your checkers wait off the board, and are lit. Dice 1 and 2.

enterAll.title: Enter all 15 first
enterAll.body: Now each die enters one more checker. A double enters four, all on the same point. Your checkers on the board wait until all 15 are in. You rolled 3-3: enter your last four checkers on point 22.
enterAll.hint: The checkers on the board cannot move yet. Enter a waiting checker on point 22.
enterAll.done: All 15 are in! Now your army may move on.
enterAll.board: Board. 11 of your checkers are on points 20 to 24. 4 more wait off the board, and are lit. Dice 3-3.

quarterLock.title: Quarter by quarter
quarterLock.body: Your path has four quarters of six points. A checker that moves into a new quarter is frozen there until all 15 have reached it. Your 14 checkers on points 14 to 18 are frozen: your last checker, on point 20, holds them back. Move it up with one die. Then move any checker with the other.
quarterLock.hint: The darker checkers are frozen. First move the lit checker on point 20.
quarterLock.done: All 15 were in one quarter again, so your army could move on. Your last checker sets the pace.
quarterLock.board: Board. Your last checker, on point 20, is lit. Your other 14 checkers are on points 14 to 18, frozen. Dice 4 and 3.

pinLast.title: Pin the last checker
pinLast.body: There is no hitting in Asodio: you pin, as in Plakoto. Your opponent’s last checker sits alone on point 10, and the rest of their army waits for it, frozen. Pin it with the lit checker.
pinLast.hint: Move the lit checker 6 points, onto the dark checker on point 10.
pinLast.done: Pinned! Your opponent’s last checker cannot move, so their whole army is frozen. They pass until you leave point 10.
pinLast.board: Board. Your checker on point 16 is lit. Your opponent’s last checker sits alone on point 10. Their other checkers are on points 13 and 14, frozen. Dice 6 and 2.

end.title: You know the basics!
end.body: Now play a real game of Portes against the Easy bot. The rules page has the rest.

motherCard.title: Your opponent's mother is pinned
motherCard.body: At the end of your turn, they see this card. If your mother is pinned, you get the same choice.
motherCard.resigned: Resign: you win 2 points and the game ends.
motherCard.playedOn: Play on: the game goes on. Their mother stays pinned until you leave it, and they cannot bear off.

review.nothing: No moves to review in this game.
review.intro_you: Your biggest mistakes, the biggest first.
review.intro: The biggest mistakes, the biggest first.
review.note: Best is the move the strongest bot would play.

username.title: Pick a username
username.body: Other players see it in games, invites and lists. Your account is saved, so the name stays yours.
username.label: Username
username.rules: 3 to 16 letters, digits or _. Start with a letter. Latin or Greek letters, not both.

problem.short: Too short: use at least 3 characters.
problem.long: Too long: use at most 16 characters.
problem.mixed: Use Latin or Greek letters, not both.

username.terms: I accept the terms of use
username.ageHint: We keep only that you ticked this, and when.
username.nextChange: You can change it again on {{date}}.
username.changeRule: After a change, the next one is possible in 30 days.

error.TAKEN: Another player has this name. Try another one.
error.NOT_ALLOWED: This name is not allowed. Try another one.
error.BAD_NAME: This name breaks the rules above.
error.TOO_SOON: You changed your name less than 30 days ago.
error.TERMS_NEEDED: Accept the terms of use first.
error.NOT_SAVED: A username needs a saved account: save yours in Settings → Account.
error.NOT_SIGNED_IN: You are not signed in. Open online play and sign in first.
error.failed: Could not reach the server. Try again.

username.guestOnly: A username needs a saved account. Save yours in Settings → Account. Guests play as “Guest” and a number.

choose.title: Report or block {{name}}
choose.block: Block: no new invites or games with this player, and you no longer see their name.
choose.report: Report: tell us about a bad name, cheating or harassment. A report blocks too.

blockConfirm.title: Block {{name}}?
blockConfirm.invites: You will not get invites from this player.
blockConfirm.more: Their name no longer shows to you. A game you play now goes on. You can unblock them in Settings.

reasons.title: Report {{name}}
reasons.body: What is wrong? Tap one. We read every report.
reasons.name: Offensive name
reasons.cheating: Cheating or abuse of the game
reasons.blockedAlready: You block this player already. A report tells us more.

safety.slow: This takes long. You may close this: Settings → Blocked players shows later whether it went through.

blocked.title: Player blocked
blocked.body: You will not get invites from this player. To unblock them, go to Settings → Blocked players.

reported.title: Thank you for the report
reported.body: We will look at it. You also blocked {{name}}.

failed.title: That did not work
failed.other: Check the connection and try again.
failed.tooManyBlocks: You block {{max}} players, the most you can. Unblock someone in Settings first.
failed.tooManyReports: You sent {{max}} reports in the last 24 hours, the most you can. Try again tomorrow.
failed.signedOut: You are not signed in to online play on this phone.
failed.refused: The server did not take this. Close and try later.

list.failed: The list did not load. Check the connection and try again.
list.signedOut: You are not signed in to online play on this phone.
list.unblockFailed: Unblock did not work. Check the connection and try again.

username.text: Friends find you by it, and they see it in each game.

invites.text: Invite a friend from your list. They get a notification if they turned them on.
